identity_constraint.note: Only 2 real users exist in the account: joemarie@kissflow.com (a member of ALL 6 app roles — Project Manager, Team Member, Department Head, Project Sponsor, PSC Member, Hub Administrator) and charumathi@kissflow.com (a member of NO app role). The runtime API is authenticated by a single account-level access-key credential (KF_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET), not a per-user session, and there is no impersonation mechanism available to this agent. This means: (a) any positive action the API CAN perform is not proof that only the intended role can perform it, and (b) any role-scoped denial cannot be behaviorally proven live — there is no second credentialed user to attempt the denied action as. These are flagged per-scenario below as observed vs. structural-only vs. untested.

blockers.summary: The runtime Form/Case create and update APIs silently drop (200, field absent on read-back) OR 500-crash on every payload shape tried for a required Reference field pointing at a real record in another flow. Tried on ITPMD_Cost_Entry_A00.project -> ITPMD_Project_A00: {_id}, {_id,Name}, {_id,Name,Kind:'Form'/'Model'}, {Id}, plain id string, arrays of the above -- via draft-create, batch-create (_is_created:true), and post-create update. Plain string / array shapes return HTTP 500 'unexpected error'; object shapes return 200 but the field is never persisted, and Form submit then 400s 'project: Value is required'. Case (Issue/Action Item) validates the same Reference at create time and rejects immediately with the identical error.
blockers.impact: Blocks live creation of ANY project-linked record via this API: Activity, Risk, Cost Entry, Issue, Action Item, and the PSR-to-Project link all require this same Reference type. This is the reason priorities 2 (board status moves) and most of 3/4 could not be run end-to-end with a real linked Project.
blockers.owner: kf-data-architect / engine (client.mjs runtime-write layer) -- needs the real Reference-write shape confirmed against a working live app, or a platform-side fix.
blockers.note: PSR (a Process) was the one exception: its own required 'project' Reference is NOT enforced at create/submit time the same way (create+submit both returned 200 despite the identical silent-drop), which is how the PSR submit journey below could be run at all -- but the resulting PSR items are also unlinked to any Project.

blockers.summary: Submitting a PSR item forward past the PM-owned Draft step works (200 'Submitted successfully', _current_step correctly becomes 'Department Head Review'). Submitting the SAME item's Department Head Review UserTask -- using the freshest correct activity-instance-id read from _current_context immediately beforehand -- consistently 400s: KISSFLOW_ERROR_050302 'You don't have permission to submit this item anymore' (stale id) or KISSFLOW_ERROR_050201 'This item has moved out of your queue' (fresh id, tried twice on two separate PSR items). No claim/pick/self-pick endpoint exists (/claim, /pick, /self-pick, /selfpick all 404).
blockers.impact: J-09, J-12, J-13 (DH return, PM resubmit, DH approve incl. BR-10 routing, PS approve) could NOT be exercised live -- the API credential can act as the process INITIATOR but not as a named approver AppRole, even though the underlying human user is a member of that role.
blockers.owner: engine (no fix available at this credential tier) -- flag to the platform owner as the still-open 'process decision-completion' question, now narrowed to an actor-identity gap rather than a URL-shape gap.

scenarios.journey: J-01 Set up a project from approved master data
steps: POST /form/2/{acc}/ITPMD_Project_A00/batch (_is_created:true) with Project_Name, Business_Unit, Portfolio, Project_Manager/Department_Head/Project_Sponsor (User), Approved_Budget, Contingency_Fund, Status
asserts: record created 200
Project_Code auto-sequenced
Currency fields stored with unit suffix
scenarios.observed: Created _id PkEGtbmUaHf1, project_code 'ITP - 0001', approved_budget '500000 USD', contingency_fund '50000 USD'. User fields required the {_id,Name,Kind:'User'} shape (plain id string / arrays rejected with InvalidUserFormat).
scenarios.finding: Project_Manager/Department_Head/Project_Sponsor User-type fields have their metadata field Id literally equal to the matching AppRole's server _id (e.g. field id 'RoEGt7NaqKtv' == Project Manager role id) on BOTH ITPMD_Project_A00 and ITPMD_Project_Status_Report_A00 -- every other User field (Risk_Owner, Responsible_Person, Issue_Owner, Assignee) got a normal snake_case id. Writes worked once the correct (role-id) key was used, so this did not block acceptance, but it is a build anomaly worth a workflow/data-architect look (possible id-collision risk).

scenarios.journey: J-02..J-07 (Activity, Risk, Cost Entry creation linked to a Project)
steps: Attempted to create Activity/Risk/Cost Entry rows with project referencing PkEGtbmUaHf1
asserts: record persists with the Project reference set
record is visible under that Project
scenarios.observed: Reference field silently dropped in every shape tried (see BLK-1). Risk and Activity records were created ANYWAY via the Form batch _is_created:true bypass (which skips required-field validation), so they exist in the sandbox but are NOT linked to the Project.

steps: Create Risk Probability=5, Impact=4 (Risk_Rating expect 20, band expect Critical)
Update Impact=5 (Risk_Rating expect 25, band expect Critical)
asserts: Risk_Rating = Probability*Impact
Risk_Rating_Band reflects the >=20 Critical threshold
scenarios.observed: Risk_Rating computed and RECOMPUTED correctly both times (20, then 25 after update -- single-level formula is fine). Risk_Rating_Band stayed 'Low' both times (should be 'Critical' at >=20). Root cause: Risk_Rating_Band is a formula-of-a-formula (reads Risk_Band_Code, which reads Risk_Rating) and that second level never (re)computes on create or update.

scenarios.journey: Priority 3: Activity create/update by PM and Team Member
steps: Update Percent_Complete to 40 (simulating the Team Member's own-record edit)
asserts: Planned_Duration_Days = DATEDIFF
Weighted_Complete_Value = %complete*duration/100
Status text reflects Not Started / In Progress
scenarios.observed: Planned_Duration_Days=14 (correct) and Weighted_Complete_Value 0 then 5.6 after update (correct, 40*14/100). Status stayed 'In Progress' at both 0% and 40% complete with Actual_Start blank -- formula says Status_Code should be 1 ('Not Started') until Actual_Start is set. Same chained-formula-of-formula defect as the Risk finding above.
scenarios.untested_note: Could not test the field-level restriction 'Team Member edits only %Complete of their own Activity' (decisions.md D20's known residual: Forms have no per-step field_permissions) -- confirmed as a documented gap, not exercised further since the same single identity can write ANY field regardless.

scenarios.journey: J-08 Generate, preview and submit the monthly PSR
asserts: item advances from Draft to Department Head Review
_status becomes InProgress
_current_assigned_to becomes Department Head
scenarios.observed: Two independent PSR items (PkEGtj2c_B95, PkEGtlASsP7u) both created and submitted 200; GET .../{item}/{aiid}?_response_type=full confirmed _current_step:'Department Head Review', _status:'InProgress', _current_assigned_to:[Department Head role]. This is real, observed forward-workflow movement, not a simulated pass.
scenarios.caveat: Both PSR items are unlinked to a Project (BLK-1), so the auto-populated schedule/risk/financial sections (ITPH-0094/0095) could not be verified -- only the submit-and-advance mechanic was.

scenarios.reason: BLK-2: every attempt to complete the Department Head Review UserTask via the runtime API 400s regardless of using the freshest correct activity-instance-id (KISSFLOW_ERROR_050302 / 050201). This is a genuine actor-identity/impersonation gap in the available credential, not a scenario failure -- the DH-approval, DH-return, PM-resubmit, PS-approval and the Yes/No BR-10 routing split could not be observed. Both test PSR items remain stuck at Department Head Review in the sandbox.
scenarios.owner: orchestrator / platform owner -- needs either a per-user session credential for the Department Head/Project Sponsor identity, or confirmation of the real decision-completion mechanism.

scenarios.journey: Priority 2: Issue and Action Item board status moves
steps: POST /case/2/{acc}/ITPMD_Issue_A00 with project, issue_category, priority, issue_owner
asserts: Issue created Open
status moves Open -> In Progress -> Resolved -> Closed observed

scenarios.observed: Case creation validates the required 'project' Reference immediately server-side (unlike the PSR process) and rejected with 400 'project: Value is required' -- the same BLK-1 defect, but here it blocks creation outright (no orphaned-record bypass exists for Case the way Form batch allowed). Could not create a single Issue or Action Item, so no board status move could be attempted.

scenarios.journey: Priority 4 negative: Team Member cannot create a Cost Entry
steps: Inspected app-spec.json#permissions and #security.data_scope for (Team Member, itpmd_cost_entry)
asserts: Team Member has no Editable/ReadOnly grant on itpmd_cost_entry at all
scenarios.observed: Confirmed structurally: security.permissions and security.data_scope both have ZERO entries for (Team Member, itpmd_cost_entry) -- the role is not a member of that flow at all, matching the design intent. Could NOT be proven behaviorally: the only credential available (joemarie) is a member of ALL 6 roles simultaneously, and the account's only other user (charumathi@kissflow.com) belongs to no app role and has no separate API credential -- there is no way to attempt this create AS a Team-Member-only identity.

scenarios.journey: Priority 4 negative: Department Head cannot edit a Project
asserts: Department Head is ReadOnly, not Editable, on itpmd_project
scenarios.observed: Confirmed structurally: permissions[] lists Department Head level:'ReadOnly' scope:'my-team' on itpmd_project (apply.log's re-confirmed 200 grants match this: Member+View, no Delete). Could not be proven behaviorally for the same single-identity reason as S-NEG-tm-cost-entry.
